name: recording-login-frames

graded_by.test: core/internal/recording/ (the file is the recording lane's to name) — TestWithTheKnobOnTheLoginIsAtTheRecordingsHeadAsCodes6And7: two code-7 frames, the username then the password, before the first output frame, stamped on the core's clock, in exactly the x-login-line bytes
core/internal/recording/ (the file is the recording lane's to name) — TestWithTheKnobOffNoByteOfTheLoginIsInTheRecording: no byte of the user name or the password in either file, the knob off

description: The login frames on disk, sidecar codes 6 and 7: when policy.yaml recording.login_input is true and the session is recorded, a login supplied on session create is written at the head of the session's recording, before its first output frame, as two code-7 frames, the username then the password, stamped on the core's input clock when the core received each piece. Each frame's data is the fixed line x-login-line gives, CR LF [TSB: login answer] <text> CR LF, with the text's backslashes and C0, C1 and DEL characters escaped so the line is one printable row: here the user name corp\op is written corp\\op. A classic player prints the lines; a TSB reader knows them by their code, and they count for neither seq. A supplied login asks nothing, so there is no code-6 frame. With the knob off no byte of the login is in the recording; the bytes here are the knob-on case, and the knob-off case is the core's own test. Refused: an empty frame, data that is not the line of its code, a raw control or C1 character, a lone backslash, an escape of a character that needs none, uppercase hex, bytes that are not UTF-8, and a login frame after any other frame. The password is the synthetic constant.
